title: Tor one and a minimal graded presentation
statement: Let k be a field and S=k[x_0,x_1] with total-degree grading [def-sc-p1-standard], let S_+=(x_0,x_1), and let N be a finitely generated graded S-module [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Let q:F\to N be a finite graded free presentation such that the induced map F/S_+F\to N/S_+N is an isomorphism, and put K=ker(q). Then there is a natural isomorphism Tor_1^S(N,k)\cong K/S_+K. Consequently Tor_1^S(N,k)=0 implies K/S_+K=0.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-p1-tor-kernel-boundary-natural] to R=S, M=k and each surjection q:F -> N. This provides boundary maps delta_P:Tor_1(N,k) -> ker(q) tensor k, exact at Tor_1(N,k) and ker(q) tensor k, with naturality in every commuting presentation square.

proof.text: The basis of F makes it projective. By [lem-sc-p1-tor-free-vanishing], Tor_1(F,k)=0; exactness at Tor_1(N,k) shows the boundary is injective. Minimality applied to q(x)=0 puts every x in ker(q) inside S_+F. Since constant coefficient kills each variable, it kills S_+; induction on ideal multiples shows x tensor z=0 in F tensor k. Thus the tensor of the kernel inclusion is zero. Exactness at ker(q) tensor k shows the boundary is surjective.

proof.text: Construct the residue equivalence S/S_+ -> k by constant coefficient; its inverse is induced by constant polynomials, as seen by polynomial ring-hom extensionality on constants and variables. The right-tensor form of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring] identifies ker(q) tensor k with ker(q)/S_+ker(q). Compose its inverse with the inverse bijective boundary. The inverse quotient identification sends [x] to x tensor 1; applying boundary naturality and the formula for c tensor 1 proves the requested equality. An injective equivalence transports subsingletonness.

lean.statement: theorem exists_minimalPresentationTor_equiv (k : Type v) [Field k] : let S := MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k let I : Ideal S := Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin 2 → S)) let residue : ModuleCat.{v} S := (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (constantCoeff : S →+* k)).obj (ModuleCat.of k k) let T := Tor' (ModuleCat.{v} S) 1 ∃ e : ∀ P : MinimalGradedPresentation k, (LinearMap.ker P.q ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule S (LinearMap.ker P.q)))) ≃ₗ[S] ((T.obj P.N).obj residue), (∀ P : MinimalGradedPresentation k, Subsingleton ((T.obj P.N).obj residue) → Subsingleton (LinearMap.ker P.q ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule S (LinearMap.ker P.q))))) ∧ (∀ (P Q : MinimalGradedPresentation k) (a : P.F →ₗ[S] Q.F) (b : P.N →ₗ[S] Q.N) (c : LinearMap.ker P.q →ₗ[S] LinearMap.ker Q.q), (∀ (j : ℤ) (x : P.F), x ∈ P.fGrading j → a x ∈ Q.fGrading j) → (∀ (j : ℤ) (x : P.N), x ∈ P.nGrading j → b x ∈ Q.nGrading j) → Q.q.comp a = b.comp P.q → (∀ x : LinearMap.ker P.q, (c x : Q.F) = a (x : P.F)) → ∀ x : LinearMap.ker P.q, ((T.map (ModuleCat.ofHom b)).app residue).hom (e P ((I • (⊤ : Submodule S (LinearMap.ker P.q))).mkQ x)) = e Q ((I • (⊤ : Submodule S (LinearMap.ker Q.q))).mkQ (c x)))
